name: Accounting
title: Bookkeeper
blurb: Accounting is the language every SAP FI/CO project, markets-system P&L and consulting case is written in, and 簿記 certificates are a credential Japanese employers recognise instantly.

chapters.title: Double-entry and journals
chapters.read: A 日商簿記3級 textbook's opening chapters on 仕訳, 勘定科目 and 転記: the five account groups (assets, liabilities, net assets, revenue, expenses), which side each increases on, and how journals post to the general ledger and trial balance (試算表).
chapters.produce: Journalise 25 transactions for a small café's first month in Japanese account names, post them to T-accounts and prepare a balancing trial balance.

chapters.title: The three statements and how they link
chapters.read: An introductory financial accounting text's chapters on the balance sheet (貸借対照表), income statement (損益計算書) and cash flow statement (キャッシュ・フロー計算書), focusing on how net income flows to retained earnings and how the indirect method reconciles profit to operating cash flow.
chapters.produce: Take one Japanese listed company's 決算短信 summary figures and draw a one-page diagram showing how net income, retained earnings, cash and the three cash flow sections connect, with the actual numbers.

chapters.title: Accruals and deferrals
chapters.read: A 簿記3級 textbook's chapter on 経過勘定 (前払費用, 未払費用, 前受収益, 未収収益) and 再振替仕訳, with the accrual principle that revenue and expenses belong to the period they relate to, not the period cash moves.
chapters.produce: For ten realistic year-end situations (insurance, rent, interest, wages) write the adjusting entry and the following year's reversing entry, with month-count working shown.

chapters.title: Depreciation
chapters.read: A 簿記3級/2級 textbook's chapters on 有形固定資産 and 減価償却: straight-line (定額法) and declining-balance (定率法) methods, monthly pro-rating for mid-year purchases, the indirect method with 減価償却累計額, and gains and losses on disposal.
chapters.produce: Build a spreadsheet depreciation schedule for three assets (one bought mid-year, one on declining balance, one sold in year three) that outputs annual expense, accumulated depreciation, book value and the disposal entry.

chapters.title: Inventory: FIFO and weighted average
chapters.read: A 簿記3級/2級 textbook's chapters on 商品有高帳 and 売上原価: first-in first-out (先入先出法), moving average (移動平均法) and periodic weighted average (総平均法), plus the 三分法 closing entries that compute cost of sales.
chapters.produce: Fill in a 商品有高帳 (stock ledger) for one month of purchases and sales twice, once with FIFO and once with moving average, and reconcile COGS + ending inventory to goods available for sale.

chapters.title: Receivables, payables, bad debts and provisions
chapters.read: A 簿記3級/2級 textbook's chapters on 売掛金・買掛金, 手形 and 貸倒引当金 (差額補充法), followed by an intermediate text's section on provisions (引当金, IAS 37 recognition criteria) such as bonus and warranty provisions.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page 'receivables to bad debt' walkthrough with entries for a credit sale, a note received, a write-off of a prior-year and a current-year debt, and the year-end allowance top-up.

chapters.title: 簿記3級 closing and the 精算表
chapters.read: A 簿記3級 textbook's 決算 chapters: the standard 決算整理事項 (現金過不足, 貯蔵品, 売上原価, 貸倒引当金, 減価償却, 経過勘定), the 8-column 精算表, and closing entries through the 損益 account to 繰越利益剰余金. Then do several timed past-style 第3問 problems.
chapters.produce: Complete three full 精算表 problems from a 簿記3級 problem book under exam timing, and keep an error log of every mistake by type.

chapters.title: Consolidated accounts basics (簿記2級)
chapters.read: A 簿記2級 商業簿記 textbook's 連結会計 chapters: 投資と資本の相殺消去, のれん, 非支配株主持分, elimination of intra-group balances and 未実現利益, plus the idea of control versus significant influence (持分法).
chapters.produce: Prepare a consolidation worksheet for a parent and an 80% subsidiary at acquisition and one year later, showing goodwill, NCI, intra-group eliminations and the consolidated balance sheet.

chapters.title: Tax-effect accounting (税効果会計)
chapters.read: A 簿記2級 textbook's 税効果会計 chapter: temporary versus permanent differences, 繰延税金資産 and 繰延税金負債, 法人税等調整額, and the treatment of その他有価証券評価差額金.
chapters.produce: For five temporary differences (excess bad debt provision, excess depreciation, securities revaluation, and two of your choice) write the origination and reversal entries and show how reported tax expense comes to the statutory rate times pre-tax profit.

chapters.title: Industrial bookkeeping basics (工業簿記)
chapters.read: A 簿記2級 工業簿記 textbook's early chapters: 材料費・労務費・経費, direct versus indirect costs, 製造間接費 and predetermined overhead rates with 配賦差異, the flow from 仕掛品 to 製品, and an introduction to 総合原価計算 with equivalent units.
chapters.produce: Draw the full 工業簿記 account flow (材料 → 仕掛品 → 製品 → 売上原価, with 製造間接費) for a small furniture maker and fill in one month of numbers that tie to a 製造原価報告書.

chapters.title: J-GAAP vs IFRS and revenue recognition
chapters.read: An overview from a Big Four firm's or the ASBJ's comparison material on J-GAAP versus IFRS (goodwill, extraordinary items, presentation), then the five-step model of IFRS 15 and Japan's 収益認識に関する会計基準, including performance obligations and principal versus agent.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page comparison table of the ten J-GAAP vs IFRS differences you would most likely meet on an SAP FI project, and work through three five-step revenue examples (bundle, subscription, agent sale).

chapters.title: Japanese specifics: 消費税, インボイス, 電子帳簿保存法
chapters.read: A 簿記3級/2級 textbook's 消費税 (税抜方式) section with 仮払消費税・仮受消費税・未払消費税, then the National Tax Agency's plain-language guides to the qualified invoice system (インボイス制度) and the electronic record-keeping law (電子帳簿保存法), focusing on the core rules.
chapters.produce: Journalise a month of sales and purchases for a café with mixed 8% and 10% items using the tax-excluded method, compute the consumption tax payable, and list which fields a 適格請求書 must contain.

name: SQL & Data
title: Data Wrangler
blurb: Every target role needs data skills: consultants analyse client data in Excel and SQL, and SAP and Murex/Calypso projects live on queries, reconciliations, batch jobs and test evidence.

chapters.title: SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY
chapters.read: A free interactive SQL tutorial's first lessons (e.g. on SQLite or PostgreSQL): SELECT columns, WHERE with AND/OR/IN/BETWEEN/LIKE, IS NULL, ORDER BY ASC/DESC, LIMIT, and the logical order in which a query is evaluated.
chapters.produce: Load a 50-row CSV of your own expenses into SQLite and write 15 queries answering real questions (e.g. 'all food spending over ¥1,000 in May, largest first').

chapters.title: JOINs
chapters.read: The JOIN lessons of a free SQL tutorial: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER and CROSS joins, join keys, table aliases, finding unmatched rows, and the difference between filtering in ON and in WHERE.
chapters.produce: Create customer, order and product tables in SQLite and write 10 join queries, including 'customers with no orders' and 'orders whose customer is missing', checking each row count by hand.

chapters.title: GROUP BY and HAVING
chapters.read: The aggregation lessons of a free SQL tutorial: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT(DISTINCT), GROUP BY with one or more columns, HAVING, and how NULLs affect aggregates.
chapters.produce: Using a public sales sample dataset in SQLite, produce a monthly sales report by region with totals, averages and order counts, and a list of regions whose sales fell below a threshold using HAVING.

chapters.title: Subqueries and CTEs
chapters.read: The subquery and WITH (common table expression) lessons of a free SQL tutorial: scalar subqueries, IN/EXISTS, correlated subqueries, NOT IN and NULL, and breaking a long query into named CTE steps.
chapters.produce: Rewrite three of your earlier multi-step analyses as single queries using CTEs, and write one correlated subquery that finds the top item in each category.

chapters.title: Window functions
chapters.read: The window function lessons of a free SQL tutorial: OVER, PARTITION BY, ORDER BY inside the window, ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG/LEAD, and running totals and moving averages.
chapters.produce: Using a year of daily prices for one stock (from a free data source) in SQLite, compute the daily return with LAG, a 20-day moving average, and each month's best day with ROW_NUMBER.

chapters.title: Excel lookups and pivot tables
chapters.read: Microsoft's free Excel training pages on VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, SUMIFS/COUNTIFS, absolute and relative references, and PivotTables.
chapters.produce: Build a workbook that looks up product prices from a master sheet with XLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH, totals sales with SUMIFS, and summarises the same data with a PivotTable, checking that both totals agree.

chapters.title: A simple 3-statement model in Excel
chapters.read: A free financial modelling tutorial on the three statements: how the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement link through net income, depreciation, working capital, capex, debt and retained earnings, with a balance check.
chapters.produce: Build a 3-year, 3-statement model for a small café in Excel from 10 assumptions (sales growth, margins, capex, depreciation, working capital days, a loan), with a balance check that is zero every year.

chapters.title: Python with pandas basics
chapters.read: The official pandas getting-started tutorials: DataFrame and Series, read_csv, selecting columns, filtering rows, loc and iloc, groupby, merge, and how missing values (NaN) are handled.
chapters.produce: In a Jupyter notebook, load a CSV of transactions, clean it, and reproduce three earlier SQL results (a filter, a GROUP BY and a LEFT JOIN) in pandas, checking that the numbers match.

chapters.title: Markets-systems tech: Unix, XML, batch and testing
chapters.read: Free beginner material on the Linux shell (ls, cd, grep, tail, wc, pipes, chmod), XML basics and simple XPath, how end-of-day (EOD) batch processing works in trading systems, and how to write a test plan.
chapters.produce: On a Linux machine or WSL, write a shell one-liner report over a sample batch log (errors per job), parse a small XML trade file with Python, and write a one-page test plan for an EOD batch change.

name: Strategy & Cases
title: Case Cracker
blurb: Strategy consulting interviews in Japan test structured thinking, フェルミ推定 and case discussion in both languages, so this is the core skill set for Arin's first-choice role.

chapters.title: Structured thinking: MECE and issue trees
chapters.read: Study a consulting problem-solving primer's chapters on MECE, issue trees and hypothesis-driven work, plus any free consulting-club guide to 'logic trees' (ロジックツリー). Key ideas: break a question into non-overlapping, complete parts; lead with a hypothesis; apply the 'so what?' test.
chapters.produce: Build three issue trees (one profit question, one 'why' question, one 'how' question) at least three levels deep, and mark the branch you would test first with a one-line hypothesis.

chapters.title: Business frameworks: 3C, 4P, five forces, value chain
chapters.read: Read a strategy textbook's chapters on Porter's five forces and the value chain, and a Japanese marketing primer's sections on 3C分析 and 4P (マーケティング・ミックス). Key idea: frameworks are checklists for building a tailored structure, not answers to recite.
chapters.produce: Apply 3C, 4P and five forces to one Japanese company you know (e.g. a konbini chain) on a one-page sheet each, ending each page with one 'so what' line.

chapters.title: Profitability trees
chapters.read: Study a case-interview guide's chapter on profitability, plus a 簿記3級 or management-accounting textbook's section on fixed vs. variable costs and contribution margin. Key ideas: Profit = (Price - Variable cost) x Volume - Fixed cost; segment before you conclude.
chapters.produce: Draw a full profitability tree for a ramen chain and fill it with made-up but consistent numbers, then write a three-line diagnosis of where profit leaked.

chapters.title: Market sizing (フェルミ推定)
chapters.read: Work through a Japanese フェルミ推定 workbook's opening chapters and a case guide's market-sizing section. Key ideas: choose demand-side (population down) or supply-side (stores x capacity), segment the population, keep round numbers, and sanity-check with a second method.
chapters.produce: Solve 10 Fermi problems on paper in under 5 minutes each (e.g. konbini coffee cups per year in Japan), showing the tree and a sanity check for each.

chapters.title: Mental math for cases
chapters.read: Practise with a case-math drill book or free case-math drill sites: percentages, growth rates, CAGR, break-even, the rule of 72, and handling zeros (万, 億, million, billion). Key idea: round sensibly, say your steps aloud, and state units.
chapters.produce: Do 15 minutes of timed case math daily for two weeks and log your speed and accuracy; finish with a self-made sheet of 30 problems at 90%+ accuracy.

chapters.title: Case types: profitability, market entry, growth
chapters.read: Read a case-interview book's chapters on profitability, market entry and growth cases, and practise with free case books from university consulting clubs. Key ideas: tailored structure, entry modes (build, buy, partner), the Ansoff matrix, payback.
chapters.produce: Run six full practice cases (two of each type) with a partner or out loud alone, recording each and writing a one-paragraph self-review.

chapters.title: Case types: M&A and PE due diligence, pricing, operations
chapters.read: Study a case guide's chapters on M&A, private-equity due diligence, pricing and operations, plus a corporate-finance primer's pages on EV/EBITDA multiples. Key ideas: enterprise vs. equity value, cost vs. revenue synergies, MOIC, value-based pricing, bottlenecks.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page due-diligence checklist for a PE buyer of a Japanese regional supermarket chain, and solve one pricing and one operations case with full numbers.

chapters.title: Chart reading and clear slides
chapters.read: Study a business-presentation or data-storytelling book's chapters on action titles, chart choice and slide layout, and look at public investor-relations decks to see consulting-style slides. Key ideas: one message per slide, title states the takeaway, chart type fits the comparison.
chapters.produce: Rebuild three messy slides (from any public deck or your own work) into consulting style with action titles, and make one waterfall chart in Excel or PowerPoint.

chapters.title: Japanese industry knowledge
chapters.read: Read industry overviews in a 業界地図-style annual guide and the 'business overview' pages of large companies' integrated reports (統合報告書) for autos, electronics, 商社, convenience stores, banking and energy. Focus on structure: business models, value chains, key players and their roles, not this year's numbers.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page industry card for each of the six industries (value chain, how money is made, key players, two structural issues) and present one aloud in 3 minutes.

chapters.title: Running a case interview in Japanese and English
chapters.read: Watch firms' public case-interview example videos and read a case guide's chapter on communication; build a phrase list in both languages (clarifying, asking for time, signposting, closing). Key ideas: clarify first, think aloud with structure, synthesise with the answer first.
chapters.produce: Run four mock cases (two in Japanese, two in English) with a friend or career centre, record them, and write a 30-second closing synthesis for each.

name: Job Hunting
title: Offer Hunter
blurb: Getting into a Japanese consulting firm means passing ES screening, web tests, video interviews and group discussions in the 就活 system, often before any case or technical interview.

chapters.title: Japan's new-graduate hiring flow
chapters.read: Read a 就活 guidebook's opening chapters and your university career centre's materials for international students on 新卒一括採用, インターンシップ, 説明会, ES, web tests, interviews, 内々定 and 内定, plus the visa change after an offer. Key idea: the order of steps and the alternative routes (通年採用, autumn entry) for non-April graduates.
chapters.produce: Draw your own hiring-flow map with target firms in each of your three role types and the route each one offers (new-grad, year-round, internship-linked), and book one career-centre consultation.

chapters.title: Aptitude tests: SPI, 玉手箱, TG-WEB
chapters.read: Work through an SPI 問題集 (言語 and 非言語) and a 玉手箱 / TG-WEB 問題集, focusing on 損益算, 速さ, 割合, 仕事算, 四則逆算, 図表の読み取り and 数列. Key idea: speed comes from recognising the question type instantly.
chapters.produce: Complete two full timed mock tests for each of SPI and 玉手箱, log your error types, and redo every missed question until you can solve it in under one minute.

chapters.title: エントリーシート in English and Japanese
chapters.read: Read an ES-writing guide's chapters on 志望動機, 自己PR and ガクチカ, and the English-resume section of your career centre's guide. Key ideas: 結論ファースト, specific evidence, consistent style (です・ます or である), and respecting character limits.
chapters.produce: Write a 400字 志望動機 and a 400字 自己PR in Japanese, plus a 200-word English version of each, and get them reviewed by a career-centre adviser or a Japanese friend.

chapters.title: STAR stories and ガクチカ
chapters.read: Study an interview-preparation guide's section on behavioural questions and STAR, and a Japanese guide's chapter on ガクチカ and 深掘り questions. Key ideas: most time on Action, clear personal role, measurable Result, and why you made each choice.
chapters.produce: Build a bank of five STAR stories (leadership, teamwork, failure, problem solving, working across cultures), each with a 1-minute English and 1-minute Japanese version, and answer five 'why?' follow-ups for each.

chapters.title: HireVue and video interviews
chapters.read: Read the candidate guide that video-interview platforms and employers publish, and your career centre's notes on recorded interviews. Key ideas: one-way recorded answers, prep time and answer time limits, camera, light, sound, and short answer-first structure.
chapters.produce: Record yourself answering ten common questions (five in English, five in Japanese) with a 30-second prep and 60-second answer limit, then review and re-record your three weakest answers.

chapters.title: Group discussions (グループディスカッション)
chapters.read: Read a 就活 guide's chapter on グループディスカッション and watch public example GD videos. Key ideas: roles (司会, 書記, タイムキーパー), the flow (define the goal, generate ideas, set criteria, decide, present), and contributing to the team's result.
chapters.produce: Take part in at least three practice GDs (career centre or study group), and after each one write down your contributions, one phrase you used well and one you want to add.

name: Business Japanese
title: Keigo Speaker
blurb: Japanese consulting interviews and client work run on keigo, structured reporting and business email, so Arin needs these to move from N4-N3 classroom Japanese to working Japanese.

chapters.title: Keigo: 尊敬語, 謙譲語, 丁寧語
chapters.read: Study a business-Japanese textbook's keigo chapters or an N3-N2 grammar book's keigo section: the special verbs (いらっしゃる, おっしゃる, 召し上がる, 申す, 参る, 伺う, 拝見する), お/ご～になる and お/ご～する patterns, and the 内/外 rule. Key idea: raise the other person (尊敬語), lower yourself and your company (謙譲語).
chapters.produce: Make a 30-verb keigo table (plain / 尊敬語 / 謙譲語) and write ten sentences about your own boss speaking to an outside client, then have a Japanese speaker check them.

chapters.title: Business email structure and set phrases
chapters.read: Read a business-email phrasebook or a business-Japanese textbook's email chapter: 件名, 宛名, 挨拶, 名乗り, 本文, 結び, 署名, and set phrases for requests, thanks, apologies and confirmation. Key idea: the frame is fixed; only the 本文 changes.
chapters.produce: Write five emails to a company's HR department (interview scheduling, thanks after an interview, rescheduling, a question, accepting an offer) using the full structure, and get them checked.

chapters.title: 自己紹介 and 自己PR
chapters.read: Study a 就活 interview book's chapter on 自己紹介 and 自己PR, and a business-Japanese textbook's self-introduction unit. Key ideas: 自己紹介 is short and factual, 自己PR is answer-first (私の強みは～です) with one concrete episode, and the 御社/貴社 rule.
chapters.produce: Write and memorise a 30-second 自己紹介 and a 1-minute 自己PR in Japanese, record them, and fix pronunciation and keigo with a teacher or language partner.

chapters.title: ガクチカ storytelling in Japanese
chapters.read: Read a 就活 guide's ガクチカ chapter and model answers, and practise the connectors that carry the story (まず, そこで, その結果, この経験から). Key idea: 結論 -> 課題 -> 行動 -> 結果 -> 学び, with your reasons stated as ～と考えたからです.
chapters.produce: Write your ガクチカ in 300字 and 400字 versions, prepare spoken 1-minute and 2-minute versions, and answer five 深掘り questions in Japanese on a recording.

chapters.title: Phone and meeting phrases
chapters.read: Study a business-Japanese textbook's telephone and meeting units: answering, saying someone is away, taking messages, asking someone to repeat, and politely disagreeing in meetings. Key idea: set phrases plus the 内/外 rule for colleagues' names.
chapters.produce: Role-play ten phone calls and two short meetings with a language partner using a phrase sheet you made, and record one call to check speed and politeness.

chapters.title: The pyramid principle and 結論から speaking
chapters.read: Read a book on the pyramid principle or logical writing (ロジカル・ライティング) and a Japanese business-communication guide's sections on PREP法 and 報連相. Key ideas: the main message on top, supporting points grouped and MECE, SCQA for introductions, conclusion first when reporting.
chapters.produce: Rewrite three of your own long emails or reports as pyramids (one top message, three grouped supports), and give a 1-minute PREP report in Japanese on a topic of your choice.

chapters.title: English business writing
chapters.read: Study a plain-English business-writing guide's chapters on BLUF, concise sentences, active voice, subject lines and parallel bullet points, and compare a few consulting-style emails. Key idea: the reader should know what you want from the subject line and first sentence.
chapters.produce: Rewrite five of your own English emails or reports using BLUF and active voice, cutting each by at least 30% in words, and write a one-page memo with a recommendation and three supporting bullets.

name: Corporate Finance & Valuation
title: Valuation Analyst
blurb: Valuing companies and projects is the shared language of strategy consulting cases, SAP FI/CO controlling work and the trading desks that Murex and Calypso serve.

chapters.title: Time value of money
chapters.read: A corporate finance textbook's opening chapters on compounding, discounting, annuities and perpetuities; practise each formula alongside Excel's FV, PV and PMT functions.
chapters.produce: Build an Excel sheet that computes FV, PV, annuity PV and a loan payment for any rate and term, and check it by hand against 5 worked cases.

chapters.title: NPV, IRR and payback
chapters.read: The capital budgeting chapter of a corporate finance textbook: NPV, IRR, payback and why NPV is the preferred rule; practise with Excel's NPV and IRR functions.
chapters.produce: Evaluate three hypothetical projects for a Yamanashi winery (NPV, IRR, payback) in one spreadsheet and write a one-paragraph recommendation.

chapters.title: Cost of capital: CAPM and WACC
chapters.read: A corporate finance textbook's chapters on risk and return, beta, CAPM and the weighted average cost of capital, including the tax shield on debt and market-value weights.
chapters.produce: Estimate the WACC of one listed Japanese company: take its beta, an assumed risk-free rate and market premium, and its market cap and debt, and document every input.

chapters.title: Free cash flow and building a DCF
chapters.read: A valuation textbook or investment-banking training guide's chapters on unlevered free cash flow, forecasting revenue, margins, capex and working capital, and the bridge from enterprise value to equity value.
chapters.produce: Build a 5-year DCF for a simple listed company in Excel: revenue drivers, UFCF, discounting at WACC and an EV-to-equity bridge ending in a value per share.

chapters.title: Terminal value and sensitivity
chapters.read: A valuation textbook's chapter on terminal value (Gordon growth versus exit multiple), discounting it correctly and building sensitivity tables with Excel data tables.
chapters.produce: Add both terminal value methods to your DCF and a 5×5 WACC-versus-growth sensitivity table, then write three sentences on what drives the value.

chapters.title: Trading and transaction comparables
chapters.read: A valuation textbook's chapter on relative valuation: choosing peers, calculating EV and equity value, EV/EBITDA, P/E and EV/sales, and how precedent-transaction multiples differ.
chapters.produce: Build a comps table for 5 Japanese listed peers in one sector (EV, EBITDA, EPS, multiples, median), and value a sixth company from the median.

chapters.title: Reading 決算短信 and 有価証券報告書
chapters.read: Download one company's 決算短信 (from its IR page or TDnet) and its 有価証券報告書 (from EDINET), and map the Japanese P&L lines (売上高 to 当期純利益), the balance sheet, the cash flow statement and the segment notes to their English equivalents.
chapters.produce: Make a bilingual one-page cheat sheet of 30 key line items and section names, then extract 5 years of 売上高, 営業利益 and 営業CF for one company into a spreadsheet.

chapters.title: M&A basics: synergies, accretion and dilution
chapters.read: An M&A or investment-banking textbook's chapters on deal rationale, control premiums, valuing synergies, goodwill, and building an accretion/dilution analysis for stock and cash deals.
chapters.produce: Build a one-sheet accretion/dilution model for a hypothetical all-stock acquisition between two Japanese companies, with a toggle for synergies.

name: Management Accounting
title: Controller
blurb: SAP CO is management accounting in software form, and cost, margin and break-even thinking is the backbone of every strategy-consulting case.

chapters.title: Cost behaviour, CVP and break-even
chapters.read: A management accounting textbook's chapters on fixed, variable and mixed costs (the high-low method), contribution margin and cost-volume-profit analysis, including target profit and margin of safety.
chapters.produce: Build a one-sheet CVP model for a ramen shop (price, variable cost per bowl, monthly fixed costs) that outputs break-even bowls, target-profit volume, margin of safety and a break-even chart.

chapters.title: Cost centres, profit centres and internal orders
chapters.read: A management accounting text's chapter on responsibility accounting, then SAP Learning (learning.sap.com) material on overhead cost controlling in S/4HANA: cost centres, cost elements, activity types, internal orders and settlement, and profit centres.
chapters.produce: Design a cost-centre and profit-centre hierarchy for a fictional 200-person manufacturer, with two service cost centres allocated by drivers you choose and one internal order for a trade fair settled to marketing.

chapters.title: Product costing: job and process
chapters.read: A cost accounting textbook's chapters on job-order costing, process costing with equivalent units, and absorption versus variable costing, then SAP Learning material on product cost planning (BOM, routing, cost estimate).
chapters.produce: Cost one custom job and one month of a bottling process by hand, then write a half-page note on how SAP would get the same numbers from a BOM, routing and activity prices.

chapters.title: Standard costing and variance analysis
chapters.read: A cost accounting textbook's 標準原価計算 chapter: setting standards, material price and quantity variances, labour rate and efficiency variances, and who is responsible for each.
chapters.produce: Take one month of plan versus actual data for a product and write a variance report that splits the total cost variance into price/quantity and rate/efficiency, with a sentence on the likely cause of each.

chapters.title: Budgeting
chapters.read: A management accounting textbook's budgeting chapters: the master budget sequence (sales, production, materials, labour, overhead, cash), flexible budgets, and alternatives such as zero-based budgeting.
chapters.produce: Build a linked quarterly master budget in a spreadsheet for a small manufacturer, from sales budget through to a cash budget that flags months needing a bank loan.

chapters.title: Profitability analysis by segment
chapters.read: A management accounting textbook's chapter on segment reporting and the contribution approach (contribution margin, traceable fixed costs, segment margin), then SAP Learning material on margin analysis / CO-PA characteristics and value fields.
chapters.produce: Build a segment P&L for a company with three regions and two products, showing contribution margin and segment margin by cell, and write a short recommendation on which segment to fix or exit.

name: ERP & SAP FI/CO
title: FI/CO Specialist
blurb: SAP FI/CO is one of Arin's three target roles, and Japanese SAP consultancies hire graduates who can already explain how a business transaction flows through S/4HANA finance and controlling.

chapters.title: ERP concepts and end-to-end processes
chapters.read: SAP Learning (learning.sap.com) introductory journeys on S/4HANA business processes: what ERP integration means, and the steps of record-to-report (R2R), procure-to-pay (P2P, FI-MM) and order-to-cash (O2C, FI-SD), including which steps create accounting entries.
chapters.produce: Draw three swimlane diagrams (R2R, P2P, O2C) for a small Kofu wine distributor, marking every step that posts to the G/L with its debit and credit.

chapters.title: FI enterprise structure
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on FI organisational units and global settings: company code, chart of accounts types (operational, group, country), fiscal year variants and special periods, posting period variants, document types and number ranges.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page enterprise-structure design for a fictional Japanese group with two company codes (Japan, Singapore): which chart of accounts, fiscal year variant, posting period variant and document types each uses, with a one-line reason for each choice.

chapters.title: General Ledger
chapters.read: SAP Learning journey on General Ledger accounting in S/4HANA: G/L account master data (chart-of-accounts and company-code segments), account types, open item management, reconciliation accounts, posting keys, ledgers, document splitting and the financial statement version.
chapters.produce: Design 25 G/L accounts for a small trading company (account number, name, type, open-item managed or not, reconciliation account type) and explain in writing where each would appear in the financial statement version.

chapters.title: Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable
chapters.read: SAP Learning journeys on AP and AR in S/4HANA: supplier and customer master data as business partner roles, invoices and credit memos, payment terms and cash discounts, the automatic payment program, dunning, partial and residual payments, and special G/L transactions such as down payments.
chapters.produce: Walk one supplier invoice and one customer invoice through their full life on paper (invoice, payment proposal or dunning, payment, clearing), writing the journal entry at each step with consumption tax.

chapters.title: Asset Accounting (new Asset Accounting in S/4)
chapters.read: SAP Learning journey on Asset Accounting in S/4HANA: asset classes, depreciation areas and keys, acquisition, assets under construction, retirement, the depreciation run, and how new Asset Accounting posts parallel valuations in real time to the Universal Journal.
chapters.produce: Build a spreadsheet asset register for 5 assets showing monthly straight-line depreciation and one retirement with gain or loss, and write the matching SAP postings.

chapters.title: Bank Accounting
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on Bank Accounting in S/4HANA: house banks and house bank accounts, bank account management, the electronic bank statement and its posting rules, bank clearing (interim) accounts, the cash journal, and bank reconciliation.
chapters.produce: Prepare a bank reconciliation for a month with 10 bank statement lines and 3 timing differences, and map each statement line to the posting rule (debit, credit, clearing) it would trigger.

chapters.title: Period-end closing
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on financial close in S/4HANA: accruals and deferrals, foreign currency valuation, GR/IR regrouping, depreciation run, cost allocations and settlements, opening and closing periods, and balance carryforward.
chapters.produce: Write a month-end closing checklist of 15 steps for a company using FI and CO, with the order, the owner (AP, AR, GL, CO) and the check that proves each step is done.

chapters.title: CO: cost elements, cost centres and internal orders
chapters.read: SAP Learning journey on Overhead Cost Controlling in S/4HANA: the controlling area, cost elements as G/L accounts (primary and secondary), cost centres and the standard hierarchy, activity types, assessments and distributions, and internal orders with settlement rules and budgets.
chapters.produce: Set up on paper a cost centre hierarchy for a 50-person company, then allocate one month of IT and building costs to the other cost centres by headcount and floor space, and run one marketing internal order through to settlement.

chapters.title: CO: profit centres, product costing and CO-PA
chapters.read: SAP Learning journeys on Profit Center Accounting, Product Cost Planning and Margin Analysis in S/4HANA: profit centres in the General Ledger, standard cost estimates (BOM, routing, activity prices, overhead), price control S and V, variances, and account-based profitability analysis.
chapters.produce: Calculate a standard cost estimate for one product (materials, two activities, overhead), then compute the price and production variances for one month and show where they land in margin analysis.

chapters.title: S/4HANA specifics: Universal Journal, Business Partner, Fiori
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on what changed from ECC to S/4HANA in finance: the SAP HANA in-memory column database, the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA), compatibility views, the mandatory Business Partner with customer/vendor integration (CVI), and the Fiori launchpad and role-based apps.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page 'ECC vs S/4HANA Finance' comparison for a client CFO covering data model, master data and user experience, with one concrete benefit for month-end closing.

chapters.title: Migration, SAP Activate and testing
chapters.read: SAP Learning material on S/4HANA transition paths (new implementation, system conversion, selective data transition), the SAP Activate methodology and its phases, fit-to-standard workshops, data migration of master data and open items, and test types from unit to user acceptance testing.
chapters.produce: Write a 2-page migration recommendation for a fictional ECC client choosing between greenfield, brownfield and selective transition, plus a test plan listing test types, owners and exit criteria for go-live.

chapters.title: Japan setup: consumption tax, invoices and parallel ledgers
chapters.read: Japanese tax authority (国税庁) English pages on consumption tax (消費税) and the qualified invoice system (インボイス制度), plus SAP Learning material on tax codes and parallel accounting with leading and non-leading ledgers; learn the concepts only, not detailed configuration.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page note for a Japanese subsidiary explaining which tax codes it needs (10%, 8%, exempt, non-taxable), what a qualified invoice must show, and how J-GAAP and IFRS would be kept in parallel ledgers.

name: Capital Markets Products
title: Markets Specialist
blurb: Murex and Calypso consulting means configuring how banks price, book, settle and collateralise these products, so knowing each product and its trade lifecycle is the core of the role.

chapters.title: Money markets and day counts
chapters.read: An introductory financial markets textbook's chapter on money-market instruments (deposits, T-bills, CP, call money), simple interest and day-count conventions (ACT/360, ACT/365, 30/360).
chapters.produce: Write a small Excel or Python calculator that returns interest for any amount, rate, dates and day-count convention, and test it on 10 cases in USD, GBP and JPY.

chapters.title: FX spot and forwards
chapters.read: A financial markets or FX textbook's chapter on quotation conventions (base/quote currency, pips), spot value dates, cross rates and forward pricing by covered interest parity.
chapters.produce: Build a forward calculator that takes spot, two interest rates with their day counts and a tenor, and outputs the outright forward and the forward points; reproduce 5 USD/JPY and EUR/USD examples.

chapters.title: FX swaps and FX options
chapters.read: An FX or derivatives textbook's chapters on FX swaps (near and far legs, swap points, funding use) and vanilla FX options (calls and puts, strike, premium, payoff at expiry, intrinsic versus time value).
chapters.produce: Draw the payoff diagrams for a bought USD call/JPY put and a bought USD put/JPY call at strike 145, and write out the cash flows of one buy/sell USD/JPY FX swap.

chapters.title: Bonds: pricing, yield and duration
chapters.read: A fixed-income textbook's chapters on bond cash flows, pricing from yield, yield to maturity, clean versus dirty price and accrued interest, and Macaulay and modified duration.
chapters.produce: Price three JGB-style bonds in a spreadsheet from their yields, compute modified duration, and check the duration estimate against a full reprice for a 10bp move.

chapters.title: Repos
chapters.read: A money-markets or fixed-income textbook's chapter on repurchase agreements: legs, repo rate, haircuts, general versus special collateral, and how JGB repo is used for funding.
chapters.produce: Write out both legs of a 7-day JGB repo (cash amounts, dates, collateral) as you would see them in a trade ticket, including the haircut and repurchase price.

chapters.title: Interest rate swaps, caps, floors and swaptions
chapters.read: A derivatives textbook's chapters on plain-vanilla interest rate swaps (fixed and floating legs, netting, pricing from discount factors, par swap rate) and on caps, floors and swaptions as options on rates.
chapters.produce: Price a 3-year annual fixed-for-floating swap from given discount factors in a spreadsheet, and write one paragraph explaining when a client would buy a cap versus enter a payer swap.

chapters.title: TONA and the LIBOR transition
chapters.read: Bank of Japan and industry explanatory materials on TONA and risk-free reference rates, plus overview articles on the LIBOR transition, compounding in arrears and the ISDA fallbacks.
chapters.produce: Compute compounded-in-arrears TONA interest for one month of daily fixings in a spreadsheet (with weekend weighting), and write a short comparison of TONA, SOFR, SONIA and €STR.

chapters.title: Credit, equity and commodity derivatives
chapters.read: A derivatives textbook's chapters on credit default swaps (premium leg, protection leg, recovery), equity forwards and options, and commodity futures (contango, backwardation, storage costs).
chapters.produce: Make a one-page product sheet for each of CDS, equity option and commodity future, with the cash flows, who uses it and why, and one worked numeric example each.

chapters.title: Trade lifecycle and operations
chapters.read: An introduction to bank operations: the roles of front, middle and back office, and the post-trade lifecycle (trade capture, confirmation and matching, settlement and SSIs, nostro reconciliation), alongside vendor overview material on how Murex or Calypso maps these steps.
chapters.produce: Draw a swimlane diagram of an FX forward's life from execution to reconciliation, showing which office and which system does each step and which control catches which error.

chapters.title: Collateral, margin and hedge accounting
chapters.read: Overview material on the ISDA Master Agreement and the Credit Support Annex (thresholds, minimum transfer amount, eligible collateral, haircuts, variation versus initial margin), plus an IFRS 9 hedge accounting summary from an accounting firm's guide.
chapters.produce: Write a step-by-step margin-call worked example under a CSA, and a one-page summary comparing fair value hedges and cash flow hedges with one journal entry each.

name: Derivatives Pricing & Risk
title: Risk Quant
blurb: Murex and Calypso projects revolve around how swaps, FX forwards and options are priced and risk-managed, so understanding curves, Greeks, VaR and XVA lets Arin talk to traders and risk teams instead of only configuring screens.

chapters.title: Discounting and discount factors
chapters.read: A derivatives or fixed-income textbook's opening chapter on time value of money: simple, annual and continuous compounding, day-count basics (ACT/360, ACT/365), and the discount factor DF(0,T) as the price today of 1 paid at T.
chapters.produce: Build a small spreadsheet that converts one zero rate into discount factors under simple, annual and continuous compounding for maturities from 3 months to 10 years, and plot the three curves.

chapters.title: Yield curve bootstrapping and forward rates
chapters.read: The yield-curve construction chapter of a fixed-income or derivatives textbook: deposits, FRAs/futures and par swaps as curve inputs, solving discount factors one maturity at a time, interpolation, and implied forward rates.
chapters.produce: Bootstrap a 5-year annual discount curve in a spreadsheet from one deposit rate and four par swap rates, then compute the 1-year forward rates it implies and check that each input instrument reprices to par.

chapters.title: Pricing an interest rate swap
chapters.read: The interest rate swap chapter of a derivatives textbook plus a vendor or bank primer on OIS swaps: fixed and floating legs, the annuity (PV01), the par swap rate, and valuing a seasoned swap by re-pricing both legs on today's curve.
chapters.produce: Price a 5-year ¥10bn payer swap in a spreadsheet from your bootstrapped curve: leg PVs, par rate, MTM at an off-market fixed rate, and the PV change for a 1bp parallel shift.

chapters.title: Pricing an FX forward
chapters.read: The currency forwards section of a derivatives or international finance textbook: covered interest parity, forward points, outright forwards versus FX swaps, and how to value an existing forward by discounting the difference to today's forward.
chapters.produce: Build a USD/JPY forward calculator that takes spot and both currencies' rates, outputs outright and forward points for 1M–1Y, and values a seasoned forward contract.

chapters.title: Black-Scholes, put-call parity and the Greeks
chapters.read: The Black-Scholes-Merton chapter and the Greeks chapter of an options textbook: lognormal stock model, d1 and d2, call and put formulas, put-call parity, and delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho with their intuition for hedging.
chapters.produce: Implement Black-Scholes call/put prices and the five Greeks in a spreadsheet or Python, verify put-call parity numerically, and chart delta and gamma against spot for three expiries.

chapters.title: Volatility smile and surface
chapters.read: The volatility smile chapter of an options textbook and a vendor note on FX or equity vol surfaces: implied versus realised volatility, skew and smile shapes, term structure, and ATM / risk reversal / butterfly quoting.
chapters.produce: Take a set of option quotes across strikes and expiries (made-up but realistic), back out implied vols with your Black-Scholes code, and draw the smile per expiry and a simple surface table.

chapters.title: Market risk: DV01, VaR and stress tests
chapters.read: A risk management textbook's chapters on sensitivities and VaR: duration and DV01, parametric (variance-covariance) VaR, historical simulation, expected shortfall, square-root-of-time scaling, backtesting, and stress scenario design.
chapters.produce: Using two years of made-up daily P&L for a small portfolio, compute parametric and historical 1-day 99% VaR and 97.5% expected shortfall, then write a half-page stress test with three named scenarios.

chapters.title: Counterparty risk, CVA and XVA
chapters.read: A counterparty credit risk textbook's chapters on exposure (current, expected and potential future exposure), netting and collateral (ISDA/CSA), CVA as expected loss from counterparty default, and the wider XVA family: DVA, FVA, MVA, KVA.
chapters.produce: For a 5-year swap, take an assumed expected exposure profile and a flat credit spread, compute CVA in a spreadsheet, then show how it changes with netting and with a collateral agreement.

chapters.title: Regulation basics: Basel, FRTB and trade reporting
chapters.read: An introductory overview of bank regulation from a regulator's or consultancy's explainer: the Basel three pillars, risk-weighted assets and capital ratios, FRTB's standardised and internal-model approaches, central clearing, and OTC derivatives trade reporting.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page memo for a markets-systems client explaining which data a trading platform must produce for FRTB sensitivities and for trade reporting, and which teams own each.

name: Maths for Finance
title: Quant Apprentice
blurb: Calculus, matrices, statistics and random walks are the language underneath swap pricing, VaR and regression-based business analysis, so steady practice here makes the derivatives and strategy work far easier for Arin.

chapters.title: Algebra, functions, logs and exponentials
chapters.read: The first chapters of a 'maths for economics/business' textbook: solving equations, functions and their graphs, composition and inverses, exponent rules, and natural logs with applications to compound growth.
chapters.produce: Solve a 20-problem set (equations, composite functions, log rules) by hand, then build a spreadsheet showing ¥1,000,000 growing at 4% under annual versus continuous compounding for 30 years.

chapters.title: Differential calculus
chapters.read: The differentiation chapters of a maths-for-economics textbook: limits and slopes, power, product, quotient and chain rules, derivatives of e^x and ln x, and finding maxima and minima with first and second derivatives.
chapters.produce: Work 25 differentiation exercises by hand and solve two optimisation problems (profit maximisation and minimum average cost), checking each answer numerically in a spreadsheet.

chapters.title: Integral calculus
chapters.read: The integration chapters of a maths-for-economics textbook: antiderivatives, definite integrals as areas, the fundamental theorem of calculus, integrating e^x and 1/x, and applications such as present value of a continuous cash-flow stream.
chapters.produce: Work 20 integration exercises by hand and compute the present value of a continuous income stream both exactly and with a 12-step numerical approximation in a spreadsheet.

chapters.title: Linear algebra: vectors, matrices and systems
chapters.read: The matrix algebra chapters of a maths-for-economics textbook or a free linear algebra lecture series: vectors and dot products, matrix multiplication, determinants and inverses, solving linear systems, and portfolio variance as wᵀΣw.
chapters.produce: Solve five 3×3 systems by elimination and by matrix inverse (spreadsheet MINVERSE/MMULT), and compute the variance of a 3-asset portfolio from a covariance matrix.

chapters.title: Probability basics and distributions
chapters.read: The probability chapters of an introductory statistics textbook: events and rules, conditional probability and Bayes, random variables, expectation and variance, and the binomial, Poisson and normal distributions.
chapters.produce: Simulate 10,000 rolls of two dice and 10,000 binomial draws in a spreadsheet or Python and compare the simulated frequencies and means with the theoretical values.

chapters.title: Statistics: estimation, confidence intervals and tests
chapters.read: The inference chapters of an introductory statistics textbook: sample mean and standard deviation, sampling distributions and the central limit theorem, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing with z and t statistics, p-values and error types.
chapters.produce: Take a real public dataset (e.g. daily returns of a stock index you download yourself), estimate mean and volatility, build a 95% confidence interval for the mean, and test whether the mean return is zero.

chapters.title: Regression and intro econometrics
chapters.read: The simple and multiple regression chapters of an introductory econometrics textbook: OLS estimates, interpretation of coefficients, R², standard errors and t-tests, and common problems (omitted variables, multicollinearity, heteroskedasticity).
chapters.produce: Estimate a stock's beta by regressing its daily returns on an index's returns in a spreadsheet (SLOPE/LINEST or Python), report the coefficient, its t-statistic and R², and write three sentences interpreting them.

chapters.title: Intro to stochastic processes and random walks
chapters.read: An introductory chapter on stochastic processes for finance: random walks, the Markov property, Brownian motion and its independent normal increments, geometric Brownian motion for stock prices, and a first look at Itô's lemma.
chapters.produce: Simulate 1,000 paths of a symmetric random walk and of geometric Brownian motion in Python or a spreadsheet, plot 20 paths, and check that the simulated mean and variance at the end match the theory.

name: Economics
title: Economist
blurb: Strategy consultants and markets-systems people are expected to read GDP prints, BoJ decisions and yen moves fluently, and this gives Arin that language.

chapters.title: Supply, demand and elasticity
chapters.read: An introductory microeconomics textbook's chapters on supply and demand, equilibrium, price controls and price elasticity (including the midpoint method and the link between elasticity and total revenue).
chapters.produce: Pick three products you buy in Kofu (e.g. rice, train tickets, coffee) and write a one-page note on each: what shifts its demand and supply, and whether its demand is likely elastic or inelastic and why.

chapters.title: Market structures
chapters.read: A microeconomics textbook's chapters on costs, perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition and oligopoly, focusing on the MR = MC rule, entry/exit and market-concentration measures such as HHI.
chapters.produce: Write a 1-page 'industry structure' slide for a Japanese industry you can observe (convenience stores, mobile carriers or ramen shops): number of players, product differentiation, barriers to entry, and which model fits best.

chapters.title: GDP and the national accounts
chapters.read: A macroeconomics textbook's chapters on measuring GDP (expenditure, income and value-added approaches), nominal vs real GDP, the GDP deflator and GNI; then skim the structure of a Cabinet Office quarterly GDP release (速報) to see the components in practice.
chapters.produce: Build a small spreadsheet that takes C, I, G, X and M plus a deflator and outputs nominal GDP, real GDP and the growth rate, then write three sentences interpreting a made-up quarter.

chapters.title: Money, central banks and the BoJ's tools
chapters.read: A macroeconomics textbook's chapters on money, banking and monetary policy (money creation, the policy rate, open market operations), then the Bank of Japan's own explainer pages on its policy tools as concepts: policy-rate setting, quantitative easing, negative interest rates and yield curve control.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page explainer, as if for a client, of how a central-bank bond purchase flows through bank reserves, short- and long-term interest rates, and the yen; include a simple diagram.

chapters.title: Inflation, unemployment and exchange rates
chapters.read: A macroeconomics textbook's chapters on price indices (CPI), real vs nominal interest rates (Fisher equation), labour-market statistics and the Phillips curve, plus an open-economy chapter on exchange rates and purchasing power parity.
chapters.produce: Make a two-column table, 'weak yen' vs 'strong yen', listing effects on exporters, importers, tourists, households and the CPI, and write one paragraph on who in Kofu wins or loses.

chapters.title: Trade and Japan's economy
chapters.read: A textbook chapter on comparative advantage, tariffs and trade policy, then an overview of Japan's economic structure from a government white paper or an international organisation's country survey: demographics, energy dependence, manufacturing and the long period of low inflation.
chapters.produce: Write a 2-page 'Japan macro primer' a new consultant could read in 10 minutes: five structural facts, why each matters for clients, and one chart you draw yourself from published data.

name: Politics & IR
title: Policy Analyst
blurb: Consulting clients in Japan live with Diet decisions, trade rules and geopolitics, so Arin needs to explain how policy is made and how states bargain.

chapters.title: Political systems
chapters.read: An introductory comparative-politics textbook's chapters on regime types, parliamentary vs presidential systems, federal vs unitary states, constitutions and electoral systems (plurality, proportional, mixed).
chapters.produce: Draw a one-page comparison table of Japan, the UK, the US and Germany: head of state, head of government, how the executive is chosen, federal or unitary, and electoral system.

chapters.title: Japan's parliamentary system
chapters.read: An English translation of the Constitution of Japan (Chapters I, IV and V on the Emperor, the Diet and the Cabinet) plus a textbook or House of Representatives explainer on how a bill passes the Diet (国会), the cabinet (内閣) and the two houses (衆議院・参議院).
chapters.produce: Draw a flowchart of how a cabinet bill becomes law in Japan, including what happens when the two houses disagree, with the Japanese term for each body labelled.

chapters.title: International relations theories
chapters.read: An introductory IR textbook's chapters on realism (including neorealism), liberalism (interdependence and institutions) and constructivism, plus the security dilemma and basic game theory such as the prisoner's dilemma.
chapters.produce: Take one current East Asian issue and write three short paragraphs explaining it through a realist, a liberal and a constructivist lens, ending with which explanation you find strongest and why.

chapters.title: International organisations
chapters.read: The official 'about us' and founding-charter pages of the UN, WTO, IMF, ASEAN and EU, plus an IR textbook chapter on international organisations; focus on purpose, membership principles and how decisions are made.
chapters.produce: Make a one-page cheat sheet with a row per organisation (UN, WTO, IMF, ASEAN, EU): purpose, decision rule, Japan's relationship to it, and one way it could affect a consulting client.

chapters.title: Diplomacy and negotiation
chapters.read: A practical negotiation book's chapters on interests vs positions, BATNA, reservation points, ZOPA and anchoring, plus an IR textbook chapter on diplomacy (bilateral and multilateral, Track I and Track II, soft power).
chapters.produce: Prepare a negotiation plan for a realistic case (e.g. agreeing a part-time job's pay or a group project split): your interests, BATNA, reservation point, the other side's likely interests, and an opening anchor.

chapters.title: Political economy
chapters.read: An international political economy textbook's chapters on public goods and collective action, interest groups and rent-seeking, the median voter, the main IPE traditions (liberal, mercantilist/nationalist, structuralist) and the open-economy trilemma.
chapters.produce: Write a 1-page memo on why a specific protected sector (e.g. agriculture in a country of your choice) keeps its protection, using collective action and interest-group logic.

name: Music Theory
title: Arranger
blurb: A structured creative side-skill that keeps Arin's mind fresh during heavy study and trains the pattern recognition and systems thinking consulting work rewards.

chapters.title: Notation and rhythm
chapters.read: An introductory music-theory textbook's (or a free online theory course's) lessons on the staff, treble and bass clefs, note values, rests, dots and ties, time signatures and tempo markings.
chapters.produce: Transcribe the rhythm of a short melody you know (8 bars) onto staff paper or in free notation software, with correct time signature, beaming and bar lines.

chapters.title: Scales and keys
chapters.read: A theory textbook's chapters on the major scale, the three forms of the minor scale, key signatures, the circle of fifths and relative/parallel keys.
chapters.produce: Write out all 12 major scales with their key signatures in circle-of-fifths order, and play or sing at least four of them.

chapters.title: Intervals and their frequencies
chapters.read: A theory textbook's chapter on interval quality and size (major, minor, perfect, augmented, diminished, inversions), plus an introduction to equal temperament and frequency ratios (A4 = 440 Hz, ratio 2^(1/12) per semitone).
chapters.produce: Make an ear-training log: identify 50 intervals with a free interval-trainer app and record your accuracy, then build a table of the 12 equal-tempered frequencies from A4 to A5.

chapters.title: Chords and harmony
chapters.read: A theory textbook's chapters on triads (major, minor, diminished, augmented), seventh chords, inversions and the diatonic chords of a major key, with chord-symbol notation (C, Cm, Cdim, G7, Cmaj7).
chapters.produce: Spell and play all seven diatonic triads and seventh chords in C, G and F major, and label each with its Roman numeral and chord symbol.

chapters.title: Progressions and functional harmony
chapters.read: A theory textbook's chapters on harmonic function (tonic, predominant, dominant), cadences, common pop and jazz progressions (I–V–vi–IV, ii–V–I) and secondary dominants.
chapters.produce: Analyse the chords of three songs you like with Roman numerals and mark each cadence, then write your own 8-bar progression that uses at least one secondary dominant.

chapters.title: Song form and arranging basics
chapters.read: A songwriting or arranging guide's chapters on common forms (verse–chorus, AABA, 12-bar blues), section roles (intro, pre-chorus, bridge, outro), instrument ranges, transposing instruments and basic voice leading.
chapters.produce: Make a section-by-section map of one song (timings, bars, which instruments enter or drop), then arrange a 16-bar piece for three parts (melody, chords, bass) using smooth voice leading.

name: Sound Physics
title: Sound Engineer
blurb: A hands-on physics side-skill that sharpens Arin's quantitative reasoning (logs, ratios, sampling) with instant feedback through the ears.

chapters.title: Waves, frequency and wavelength
chapters.read: An introductory physics or audio-engineering textbook's chapter on sound waves: longitudinal waves, frequency, period, wavelength, the speed of sound (about 343 m/s in air at 20 °C) and the range of human hearing.
chapters.produce: Build a small table (spreadsheet or by hand) of wavelength and period for 20 Hz, 100 Hz, 1 kHz, 10 kHz and 20 kHz, and use a free tone-generator app to test the top of your own hearing range.

chapters.title: Decibels and loudness
chapters.read: An audio-engineering textbook's chapter on decibels: logarithms, dB SPL, 10·log10 for power and intensity vs 20·log10 for pressure, adding incoherent sources, the inverse-square law and equal-loudness contours.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page dB cheat sheet with worked examples (adding two sources, doubling distance, pressure vs power ratios) and check three of them with a free sound-level-meter app.

chapters.title: Harmonics and timbre
chapters.read: An acoustics or synthesis textbook's chapters on the harmonic series, standing waves in strings and pipes, waveform shapes (sine, square, sawtooth), envelopes (ADSR) and why instruments playing the same note sound different.
chapters.produce: Record the same note on two instruments or voices, view both in a free spectrum-analyser app, and write a short note comparing their harmonic content and envelopes.

chapters.title: Room acoustics
chapters.read: An acoustics or home-studio guide's chapters on reflections, absorption vs diffusion, reverberation time and the Sabine formula, room modes (standing waves) and comb filtering.
chapters.produce: Measure a room you use (your apartment or a practice room), calculate its first three axial modes for each dimension, and write a short treatment plan saying where absorption or bass traps would help most.

chapters.title: Digital audio: sampling and bit depth
chapters.read: An audio-engineering or DSP primer's chapters on sampling, the Nyquist–Shannon theorem, aliasing and anti-aliasing filters, quantisation and bit depth, dither, and PCM data rates.
chapters.produce: Export the same short recording at different sample rates and bit depths in a free audio editor, compare file sizes with your own calculations, and note what you can and cannot hear.

chapters.title: EQ, compression and mixing basics
chapters.read: A mixing guide's chapters on equalisers (high-pass, shelf, bell; frequency, gain, Q), dynamics processors (threshold, ratio, attack, release, make-up gain), masking, panning and gain staging.
chapters.produce: Mix a free multitrack session (many are offered for practice): high-pass where needed, compress the vocal, carve space for kick and bass, and write a short log of every change and why.
